HAMDEN — Town officials believe they are close to completing one of Hamden’s two overdue annual audits, temporary town Finance Director Myron Hul told the Legislative Council on Monday. Hul said completing the audits has been challenging because of bookkeeping concerns from the past. For months, town officials have sought to get a handle on Hamden’s finances as the community experiences cascading effects from late audits. These include the loss of bond credit ratings, unclear financials and coming under a new level of oversight by the state’s Municipal Finance Advisory Commission. The town has been challenged financially for years by vacancies and understaffing in its finance department and what experts have described as historically poor financial strategy by underfunding the pension fund and restructuring bond payments.
